title: hotfix: stabilize-slo-enforcer-backoff-regional-thrashing-985001
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed repeated regional thrashing during multi-region burst traffic where the SLO enforcer's backoff decisions caused oscillating regional failovers and cascading load-shedding. This PR fixes a race in the enforcer backoff ordering and adds deterministic safety measures to prevent global thrashing under bursts.

Summary of changes: atomic ordering for backoff decisions, deterministic jitter to spread retries, improved metric labels to track decision causality, a compact in-memory ordering table with CAS fallback, additional unit and integration tests, and an ops runbook update with rollout/rollback guidance.

Checklist:
- [x] Fix race condition in backoff ordering logic
- [x] Add deterministic jitter and configurable max backoff cap
- [x] Add metrics/tags for backoff decision paths (region, reason, sequence_id)
- [x] Add unit tests and an integration scenario that simulates cross-region bursts
- [x] Update Helm chart defaults to enable smoother rollout in Dedicated/Private
- [x] Add runbook section and post-deploy monitoring queries

Related tickets: Linear ENG-8473. This PR was created as an urgent hotfix after an on-call incident (SUP-2123).

Deployment notes: squash-merge to main, backport to release/2026-02 and release/2026-01. Rollout should be staged: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30 minutes with monitoring checks at each step (latency P90, failed requests by region, backoff_count metric). If increased thrashing or regression observed, revert by rolling back the deployment and tagging the instance with the previous image.

Why this change: the root cause was two simultaneous enforcers ordering backoff events without a monotonic ordering key. Under burst conditions the non-deterministic ordering caused large numbers of requests to be redirected away from a region causing capacity imbalances and further backoffs. The solution enforces a single-source-of-truth ordering path with a CAS fallback and applies small deterministic jitter to avoid synchronized retries.

CI/QA: new integration test reproduces the thrashing pattern and asserts no consecutive global failovers within a 60s window under synthetic burst traffic. Ops validated in staging for 24 hours before approval.

Notes: this is a minimal surface change focused on stability; no public API change.
